subject: Clarify package path & component swap for Wellpath (upgrade vs modular split)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@wellpath.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify package path & component swap for Wellpath (upgrade vs modular split)

Hi Marta —

Thanks for sending over the RFP. I skimmed the requirements and wanted to confirm one thing before we prepare the final pricing sheet: Wellpath is asking about two possible routes — a straight tier upgrade (move from Compact -> Core) that includes all features, or a modular composition where you keep a Compact base and add the high-throughput package + advanced observability as add-ons.

A couple of clarifying questions that will change how we recommend discounts and bundling:
- Is your primary goal predictable per-month spend (budget line-item) or predictable throughput (headroom for spikes)?
- Do you need the dedicated SLA/instance isolation right away or is that a 12–18 month objective?
- Any mandatory procurement constraints (one PO vs quarterly invoices)?

If budget predictability is the priority we typically recommend the tier upgrade (flat monthly commit with a smaller negotiated uplift). If throughput/feature control matters more, modular composition lets you buy only the add-ons you need and scale them separately — but the unit price can be higher and we typically structure that with commit tiers or a metered buffer.

I can put together two clean options (Upgrade path with proposed step-down credits, and Modular path with add-on bundles + burst pricing) and share a short one-page comparison. Sending the first draft to you by EOD tomorrow — attaching the current pricing template for reference.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Wellpath_RFP_Q3.pdf (received), redwood-pricing-proposal-v3.xlsx (draft)

Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify package path & component swap for Wellpath (upgrade vs modular split)

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the quick read. Short answers:
- Budget predictability is primary for Q4 planning (we need a committed monthly cost line on the SRE/Platform budget).
- We need isolation/SLA by Jan 2027 for the pilot (customer data regs).
- Procurement prefers a single PO per year but is open to milestone-based invoices if it helps with vendor onboarding.

If a single monthly commit is possible with a staged rollout (enable isolation for pilot in Jan and full migration by Apr), that would be ideal. We also have a pending question from security about SOC2 evidence — I can share a checklist, but there may be a short due diligence window in mid-September.

Marta Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering
Wellpath

Hi Marta —

Thanks for the quick clarify. Based on procurement needing a single PO + January SLA requirement, we recommend the following approach (short version):

Option A — Tier Upgrade (recommended):
- Move from Compact -> Core committed tier starting Jan 1
- One-year annual PO, monthly invoicing possible but priced as committed annual spend
- We offer a 12% first-year discount for the commit, plus a step-down credit if you decide to step down within the first 6 months (protects you during pilot)
- Includes dedicated SLA and priority support required for the pilot

Option B — Modular (fallback if procurement resists annual PO):
- Keep Compact base + add High-Throughput add-on + Observability add-on
- Metered burst capacity for spikes; add-ons billed monthly (higher unit rates)
- Requires explicit SLA add-on purchase for instance isolation

Next steps:
1) Ben/Jonas — can you validate the economics on Option A vs B and drop an example invoice table (monthly amortized) for Wellpath with the 12% discount and step-down credit line? I attached the pricing sheet; please fill the red cells and return.
2) Marta — I’ll include the SOC2 pointer doc in the packet and a short rollout timeline aligned to Jan/Apr.

Lauren
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Lauren / Ben —

Attached the filled pricing table and the two invoice phasing scenarios (annual committed PO amortized monthly; and modular monthly billing scenario). Key notes:
- Annual committed Core (with 12% discount) yields ~18% lower unit token cost versus modular add-ons over year 1 when measured for expected utilization (based on RFP numbers).
- Step-down credit: we propose a 3-month pro-rata credit that phases from 75% -> 50% -> 25% if they reduce commit within the first 90 days (keeps sales flexibility).
- For procurement, include a single-line purchase order template (we have one in Drive) and mark SOC2 evidence as an appendix.
